title: Reconstruction and transpose maps for integral exceptional base change
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a Cartesian square $fu=vf'$, its vertical compactification and tower adjunctions, and a canonical integral comparison datum [def-sp-exceptional-bc-integral-comparisons]. Use the actual compactification exchange and its tower counit mate [def-sp-tower-mate-data]. Define $a_K,b_K$ by composing the pullback and exceptional reduction comparisons. Define the reduction of integral compact-support exchange by conjugating the actual tower exchange by the fixed compact-support and pullback comparisons. When tower exchange is invertible, define its integral exceptional reconstruction as the inverse on Hom sets of fully faithful integral reduction applied to $a_K$, the tower mate, and $b_K^{-1}$. Given an integral compact-support exchange isomorphism, define its integral transpose by applying the adjunction for $f'$ to its inverse followed by the pulled-back counit. These constructions have real data and assert no existence or invertibility theorem.

source.place: Paragraph (3), maps a_K, b_K, reconstruction T_K and the integral transpose
